recommendation: Keep the audit commit. If this style regresses, fix or update the org.hl7.fhir.core/publisher Turtle serializer dependency rather than editing generated Turtle files in HL7/fhir.
issue_request: Applied/Persuasive R6 ITS issue requesting generated FHIR RDF Turtle examples use shorthand literal notation where equivalent, such as plain integer or boolean literals rather than quoted xsd-typed forms, with build.fhir.org/account.profile.ttl as the example and PR #1915 cited as merged.
initial_application: No HL7/fhir source commit mentioning FHIR-49946 and no checked-in generated Turtle example set were found in this checkout. The applied change is hapifhir/org.hl7.fhir.core PR #1915, merged 2025-03-03 as d6f876f8385402c60f04bc3242b75dc8508acafd, changing TurtleParser.ttlLiteral to emit shorthand for booleans, integers, and safe decimals.
additional_context: publish.ini includes rdf.html in the current build and source/rdf.html documents optional Turtle shorthand for primitive literals with caveats. Current build.fhir.org/account.profile.ttl output contains fhir:v true/false shorthand and no explicit xsd:boolean, xsd:integer, xsd:decimal, or xsd:double long-form literals in the checked Account example; xsd:nonNegativeInteger remains explicit because plain Turtle integers are xsd:integer, not that subtype. Community searches found no conflicting Zulip or Confluence evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The requested behavior is already present in current generated output through external generator code; hand-editing HL7/fhir source would not be the correct maintenance point.
